function.name: read
function.description:
Read the contents of a file at the given path. Returns up to 200 lines from the beginning by default; use offset to skip lines and limit to control how many lines to read.
Usage:
- Use this tool even if you have read the file before — file contents may have changed since your last read.
- For large files, read in chunks (offset + limit) rather than tiny 30-line slices. If you need more context, read a larger window.
- Prefer grep/glob when searching for content or files — read is for examining a specific known file.
- You can call multiple read tools in a single response — batch speculative reads that are potentially useful.
- Typically reads text files (UTF-8). Image files may also be read as visual content, depending on your capabilities. Other binary files are not supported.

offset.description: Number of lines to skip from the beginning (0-based, default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read (default: 200, max: 300)

function.name: ls
function.description: List the contents of a directory. Returns one entry per line, sorted alphabetically — directories end with "/" and files do not. Dotfiles are included.

function.name: grep
function.description:
- Fast content search tool that works with any codebase size
- Searches file contents using regular expressions
- Supports full regex syntax (eg. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+", etc.)
- Filter files by pattern with the include parameter (eg. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}")
- Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers
- Use this tool when you need to find files containing specific patterns
- If you need to identify/count the number of matches within files, use the Bash tool with rg directly if available. Do NOT use grep for counting.
- When you are doing an open-ended search that may require multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, consider delegating to a subagent instead
- You can call multiple tools in a single response — batch speculative searches that are potentially useful

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: The directory or file to search in. Defaults to the current working directory.

include.description: File pattern to include in the search (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}"). Defaults to all files.

regex.description: If true (default), pattern is a regex; if false, literal text match

max_results.description: Maximum matches to return (default: 50, hard cap: 200)

context_lines.description: Lines of context before/after each match (default: 2)

function.name: glob
function.description:
- Fast file pattern matching tool that works with any codebase size
- Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts"
- Returns matching file paths (files only, never directories)
- Respects .gitignore by default; dotfiles are included
- Use this tool when you need to find files by name patterns
- Good patterns:
  - *.ts — all files matching an extension, at any depth
  - src/*.ts — files directly inside src/ (one level, not recursive)
  - src/**/*.ts — recursive walk with a subdirectory anchor
  - **/*.py — recursive walk from the search root
  - *.{ts,tsx} — brace expansion is supported
  - {src,test}/**/*.ts — cartesian brace expansion too
- Results are capped at 100 matches; use a more specific pattern to narrow
- Avoid recursing into node_modules/, .venv/, __pycache__/ — prefer specific subpaths
- When doing an open-ended search that may need multiple rounds of globbing and grepping, consider delegating to a subagent instead
- You can call multiple tools in a single response — batch speculative searches that are potentially useful
